name: r2i_pci
prose: Builds a PROXY_CERT_INFO_EXTENSION from the configuration string value (a list of name:value settings, possibly @section references). Precondition: method may be unused; ctx is the X509V3 context used to look up sections; value is the extension string. It parses the list with X509V3_parse_list, then for every entry: an entry whose name is NULL, or whose name does not start with @ and has no value, raises X509V3_R_INVALID_PROXY_POLICY_SETTING and fails; an entry starting with @ names a section, which must exist (else X509V3_R_INVALID_SECTION) and whose values are each passed to process_pci_value until one fails; any other entry is passed to process_pci_value directly. process_pci_value (read only in part) fills the language, pathlen and policy values. After all entries, the language is mandatory (else X509V3_R_NO_PROXY_CERT_POLICY_LANGUAGE_DEFINED), and a policy together with the Independent or inheritAll language is rejected (X509V3_R_POLICY_WHEN_PROXY_LANGUAGE_REQUIRES_NO_POLICY). It then allocates the extension (ERR_R_ASN1_LIB on failure) and moves the language, policy and path length into it, so the extension owns them. Returns the new extension, or NULL on any failure, in which case the partly collected language, pathlen and policy objects and any allocated extension are freed. The parsed value list is freed on both success and failure.

name: X509_chain_check_suiteb
prose: Checks a certificate chain against the Suite B 128-bit LOS rules; returns X509_V_OK or an X509_V_ERR_SUITE_B_* code. Precondition: if x is NULL then chain must be non-NULL with the end-entity certificate as its first element; perror_depth may be NULL. If flags lacks X509_V_FLAG_SUITEB_128_LOS it returns X509_V_OK immediately. It takes the leaf key from x (or chain[0], starting the walk at index 1). With chain == NULL it only checks the leaf key algorithm and returns that check_suite_b result directly, without writing *perror_depth. Otherwise it returns X509_V_ERR_SUITE_B_INVALID_VERSION for a leaf that is not X.509 v3, then checks the leaf key, then walks the chain checking each certificate version (INVALID_VERSION) and each issuer key against the signature algorithm of the previous certificate, and finally checks the root signature. On a failure it moves the reported depth back by one (when non-zero) for INVALID_SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM and LOS_NOT_ALLOWED errors, and if the error is LOS_NOT_ALLOWED and the check changed the temporary flags (a P-384 certificate signed with P-256) it returns X509_V_ERR_SUITE_B_CANNOT_SIGN_P_384_WITH_P_256 instead. Only in the failing case with non-NULL perror_depth is *perror_depth written; on success it is left untouched. Returns X509_V_OK if all checks passed.
note: x509_cmp.c:470-544 read fully (check_suite_b not read). Original reviewer right: the chain == NULL path returns at 495-496 without setting *perror_depth. Round-15 reviewer wrong on both: *perror_depth is written only when rv != X509_V_OK (528, 540-541), and LOS_NOT_ALLOWED is remapped to CANNOT_SIGN_P_384_WITH_P_256 when flags != tflags (538-539).

name: build_chain
prose: Builds the certificate chain in ctx->chain, starting from the single leaf certificate, until a trust anchor is reached or no further issuer is found. Precondition: ctx->chain has exactly one element and ctx->num_untrusted equals 1 (otherwise internal error). Return value: 1 when the chain is trusted; 0 when trust was rejected, when a time-validity error was already reported, or when the verify callback returns 0 for a final error; -1 on an internal error (ctx->error = X509_V_ERR_UNSPECIFIED), allocation failure (X509_V_ERR_OUT_OF_MEM) or a trust store lookup failure (X509_V_ERR_STORE_LOOKUP); and, where it reports a final error through verify_cb_cert, the return value of that callback (non-zero only if the application callback chooses to continue). Search policy: it works on a shallow copy of the untrusted certificates (DANE trust anchors from DNS added first), searches the untrusted list unless none was given, and searches the trust store first when TRUSTED_FIRST is set or there is no untrusted list, with optional alternate chains (pruning untrusted certificates one at a time) unless X509_V_FLAG_NO_ALT_CHAINS; DANE without PKIX only disables the trust store search. The chain is extended by at most depth + 1 certificates. Trusted issuers replace or extend the top certificate (a self-signed untrusted certificate is replaced only by an identical trust store certificate, otherwise ignored), untrusted issuers are appended with a reference and removed from the working copy, and trust is re-evaluated with check_trust / check_dane_issuer after each addition. After the loop it tries bare DANE public-key trust and direct leaf trust when the chain is within the depth limit. For an untrusted result it reports, in order, an already recorded time error (returns 0), another preliminary ctx->error via the callback, X509_V_ERR_CERT_CHAIN_TOO_LONG, X509_V_ERR_DANE_NO_MATCH, a self-signed certificate error (DEPTH_ZERO_SELF_SIGNED_CERT for a one-element chain, else SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN) or UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT / UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY. The temporary untrusted copy is freed on all exits.

Round-15 reviewer right: the untrusted outcome ends with verify_cb_cert returns (3593, 3603-3610), i.e. 0 unless the callback overrides, not a bare success.

name: main
prose: Demo QUIC client that opens several streams on one connection and prints the responses. Precondition: command line "[-6] hostname port" (fewer than 3 arguments, or fewer than 4 with -6, prints usage and ends with EXIT_FAILURE). It creates a QUIC client SSL_CTX with peer verification and default trust paths, an SSL with default stream mode disabled, a socket BIO to the host (IPv4 or IPv6) installed with SSL_set_bio, sets SNI, hostname verification, the ALPN list and the initial peer address, and calls SSL_connect (on failure it prints the verification error if any). It then creates one bidirectional and one unidirectional stream, writes an HTTP GET request on each with write_a_request (failure ends with EXIT_FAILURE), reads and prints everything from stream 1 until SSL_read_ex fails, accepts a server-initiated stream and reads and prints it the same way. After each read loop it inspects SSL_get_error: normal end (SSL_ERROR_ZERO_RETURN) continues; a stream error of type reset or unknown, and any other error, are only printed and execution continues; a connection-closed state jumps to the end with EXIT_FAILURE. Finally it calls SSL_shutdown repeatedly until it returns 1 (a negative result ends with EXIT_FAILURE). The result is EXIT_SUCCESS only if the shutdown loop completes, so a stream read error that is merely printed can still lead to EXIT_SUCCESS. At the end label it prints the OpenSSL error stack if the result is EXIT_FAILURE, frees the SSL objects, the context and the peer address (the BIO is owned by the SSL after SSL_set_bio) and returns the result.

Round-15 and round-17 reviewers both right: reset/unknown stream failures and other read errors are only printed (330-350, 387-404) and the program can still reach EXIT_SUCCESS at 420.

name: run_quic_server
prose: Main loop of the demo HTTP/3-over-QUIC server: accepts QUIC connections on the UDP socket fd and serves one at a time. Precondition: ctx is a server SSL_CTX and fd an open UDP socket. It creates a listener (SSL_new_listener), gives it fd, starts listening and puts it in non-blocking mode (any failure goes to the error exit), sets the nghttp3 callbacks and default memory functions, and then loops forever: it waits for socket activity, reads from the connection streams until the request headers have been received (an error from the wait or from reading, or 25 consecutive timeouts, goes to the error exit; a close by the peer before a request goes to the wait-for-close step), creates the server unidirectional streams if needed, builds a 200 response with content-type and content-length derived from the requested file (a missing file gives a default test page; a file of INT_MAX length uses an endless buffer of A bytes; a file whose data cannot be loaded makes the program abort), submits the response to nghttp3 and writes the stream data out with quic_server_write until nghttp3 has nothing more to send, and then waits for the connection to close, handling new-connection, restart and done events. At the end of each iteration it closes the streams and connection and loops to accept the next connection. A failure of nghttp3_conn_submit_response, of the writes or of the offsets goes to the error exit, which prints the OpenSSL error stack, frees the listener and returns 0. The statement that sets ok = 1 is placed after the infinite loop and no break or return at the loop own level leads to it, so this function is only left through the error exit and returns 0.
note: demos/http3/ossl-nghttp3-demo-server.c:1042-1334 read fully (helpers and nghttp3 callbacks not read). Original reviewer right: ok starts at 0 and the err path returns it (1044, 1328-1333). Round-15 reviewer right: a NULL result of get_file_data calls abort() at 1179-1180 instead of returning 0. The unreachable ok = 1 (1327) is my own observation from the control flow: the only breaks at 1139, 1222, 1283, 1294, 1310 are inside inner loops.

name: OSSL_DEMO_H3_CONN_handle_events
prose: Runs one round of event handling for an HTTP/3 connection. Returns 0 if conn is NULL. Step 1: it accepts all pending incoming QUIC streams without blocking and registers each with h3_conn_accept_stream; if registration fails it frees that stream and returns 0. Step 2: it repeatedly asks nghttp3 for outgoing data (nghttp3_conn_writev_stream, up to 8 vectors) until nghttp3 has none; a negative result returns 0, and a stream id that is not in the stream map raises an internal error and returns 0. For each non-empty vector it writes the data to the QUIC stream with SSL_write_ex2 (adding the CONCLUDE flag when nghttp3 reports fin): data for a stream that was already discarded is treated as written; SSL_ERROR_WANT_WRITE is not an error, it counts 0 bytes written and blocks that stream in nghttp3 (so a vector may be only partly or not at all consumed and the function still goes on); any other write failure raises an internal error and returns 0; a successful write unblocks the stream. Whatever number of bytes was written is reported back to nghttp3 with add_write_offset and add_ack_offset (a failure returns 0). For a zero-length stream with fin it calls add_write_offset(0). Step 3: it sets conn->pump_res to 1 and runs h3_conn_pump_stream over all streams (incoming QUIC data to nghttp3); if that clears pump_res it returns 0. Returns 1 otherwise, including when some offered data could not be written because the send buffer was full.
note: demos/http3/ossl-nghttp3.c:570-712 read fully (h3_conn_accept_stream and h3_conn_pump_stream not read). Round-15 reviewer right: after SSL_ERROR_WANT_WRITE (647-653) the function does not write all data yet can still return 1 at 711. Original reviewer right that the 0/1 returns and several error paths need to be stated.

name: capi_dsa_do_sign
prose: DSA signing method of the Windows CryptoAPI engine: signs a 20-byte SHA-1 digest with the CAPI key attached to dsa and returns an OpenSSL DSA_SIG. Precondition: dsa carries a CAPI key in its ex data and its engine carries the CAPI context (neither pointer is checked before use except the key); digest points to dlen bytes. Returns NULL, with a CAPI error raised, if the key is missing (CAPI_R_CANT_GET_KEY), if dlen is not 20 (CAPI_R_INVALID_DIGEST_LENGTH), or if creating the SHA-1 hash object fails. Otherwise it loads the given digest bytes as the hash value (CryptSetHashParam; failure raises CAPI_R_CANT_SET_HASH_VALUE, returns NULL), signs the hash with CryptSignHash into a 40-byte buffer (failure raises CAPI_R_ERROR_SIGNING_HASH, returns NULL), and converts the first 20 bytes into r and the next 20 bytes into s, both read as little-endian numbers (lend_tobn), building a new DSA_SIG that owns r and s; allocation or conversion failure frees r and s and returns NULL. On all paths after the hash object was created, the signature buffer is cleansed and the hash object destroyed. The caller owns the returned DSA_SIG.
note: slice cut the head: real function capi_dsa_do_sign is engines/e_capi.c:1013-1079, read fully (lend_tobn and capi helpers not read). Round-15 reviewer right: the CAPI signature bytes are converted with lend_tobn, a little-endian conversion (1063-1064), not big-endian.

name: digest_op
prose: Issues one CIOCCRYPT ioctl on the /dev/crypto descriptor for the digest session of ctx. Precondition: ctx->sess.ses is a valid open session; src points to srclen readable bytes (it may be NULL with srclen 0); res is NULL or a buffer for the digest; flags is a COP_FLAG_* value. It fills a zeroed crypt_op with the session id, length, source pointer, a NULL destination, the mac pointer set to res and the given flags, and returns the ioctl result unchanged: 0 on success and -1 (errno set) on failure, not 1. Whether the digest is written to res depends on the kernel and the flags passed in: the callers in this file use COP_FLAG_UPDATE with res NULL (digest_update, line 777) and COP_FLAG_FINAL with the output buffer (digest_final, line 794). The function itself does not check res or flags and writes nothing else.
note: e_devcrypto.c:749-762 read fully; callers at 777 and 794 read for flags/res usage only. Reviewers: original right that the contract omitted the res side effect; round-2 right that res may be NULL (777 passes NULL); round-15 right that the digest is expected only for the FINAL call (794) and the UPDATE call writes none, as seen from the callers (the kernel behaviour itself is not visible in this source).

name: static inline int RISCV_HAS_##NAME(void)
prose: Generated function RISCV_HAS_<NAME> (from RISCV_DEFINE_CAP(NAME, INDEX, BIT_INDEX, HWPROBE_KEY, HWPROBE_VALUE) at riscv_arch.h:53-58, one static inline function per capability listed in riscv_arch.def). Takes no arguments. It returns 1 if bit BIT_INDEX of the 32-bit word OPENSSL_riscvcap_P[INDEX] is set and 0 otherwise, using the expression (OPENSSL_riscvcap_P[INDEX] & (1 << BIT_INDEX)) != 0. It only reads the global capability array, which is filled by the platform detection code elsewhere (not read here), so the result depends on that detection having run; it has no side effects. The shift is done on a plain int, so a BIT_INDEX of 31 would not be well defined; the actual values come from riscv_arch.def, which was not read.
note: macro-generated at riscv_arch.h:53-58 (read); riscv_arch.def and the code that fills OPENSSL_riscvcap_P not read. Round-17 reviewers: none (unreviewed); earlier rounds dropped it only because the name is a template.

name: nssgetpid
prose: HP NonStop replacement for getpid, defined only when building for the Guardian target (__TANDEM and _GUARDIAN_TARGET) with NO_GETPID set and NSSGETPID_MACRO not yet defined (the header defines that macro just before the definition, and afterwards maps getpid to this function). It takes no arguments. It zero-initialises a process handle array and a union that overlays a struct of two shorts (cpu, pin) with an int, calls PROCESSHANDLE_GETMINE_ to get the handle of the current process and PROCESSHANDLE_DECOMPOSE_ to extract the cpu number and pin into the struct, and returns the overlaid int as a pseudo process id. The return values of the two system calls are not checked, so if they fail the result is whatever the union holds (0 from its initialisation unless partly written). It does not touch any global state.

Round-15 reviewer right: the function is compiled only when NSSGETPID_MACRO is not yet defined (270-271), the opposite of the earlier precondition. Round-1 reviewer right that the pseudo-pid packing (cpu and pin shorts overlaid on an int) was not described.

name: ASN1_ADB_END(name, flags, field, adb_cb, def, none)
prose: Generated function <name>_adb (from the macro ASN1_ADB_END(name, flags, field, adb_cb, def, none), asn1t.h:450-465), where name is the structure name given at the use site. It takes no arguments. Precondition: a table <name>_adbtbl of ASN1_ADB_TABLE entries has been declared before it with ASN1_ADB(name), so the macro can use it in the initialiser. It returns a pointer, converted to const ASN1_ITEM *, to a function-local static ASN1_ADB structure that is initialised at compile time with the given flags, the offset of field inside name, the callback adb_cb, the table <name>_adbtbl and its element count (computed with sizeof), and the def and none default templates. The pointer is the same on every call, the pointed-to object is constant, and the function has no side effects. The macro also leaves a trailing declaration of a function named dummy_function(void) that the caller completes.

Name given as the exact macro head per rule 5; the packet name ASN1_ADB_END:name_adb refers to the generated <name>_adb function.

name: OSSL_CORE_MAKE_FUNC(type, name, args)
prose: Generated function OSSL_FUNC_<name> (from OSSL_CORE_MAKE_FUNC(type, name, args), core_dispatch.h:55-62, one per use). It takes one argument, a pointer opf to an OSSL_DISPATCH entry, and returns opf->function converted to the typedef OSSL_FUNC_<name>_fn * (a pointer to a function with return type type and parameter list args). Precondition: opf must be non-NULL (it is dereferenced without a check), and the entry should really hold a function of that signature, since the conversion is an unchecked cast. It has no side effects and does not call the function. The macro also defines the typedef OSSL_FUNC_<name>_fn.

name: int_implement_lhash_doall(type, argtype, cbargtype)
prose: Generated function lh_<type>_doall_<argtype>_thunk (from int_implement_lhash_doall(type, argtype, cbargtype), lhash.h:360-377, used by IMPLEMENT_LHASH_DOALL_ARG and IMPLEMENT_LHASH_DOALL_ARG_CONST). Takes (void *node, void *arg, OPENSSL_LH_DOALL_FUNCARG fn). It converts fn to a function pointer of type void (*)(cbargtype *, argtype *) and calls it with node cast to cbargtype * and arg cast to argtype *. Precondition: fn really has that signature (the conversion is an unchecked cast) and node and arg point to objects of the corresponding types. Returns nothing and has no other effect itself; whatever fn does is the only effect. It is used by the generated lh_<type>_doall_<argtype> function, which passes it to OPENSSL_LH_doall_arg_thunk.
